report:
Reviewed the complete semantic_query_boundaries claim, its single implementation association and its complete single-test set, plus captured review rules and architecture context. The claim has four connected obligations: boundaries represent stable semantic products; every public tracked query uses a semantic key; its result is the narrowest independently reusable product at that key; temporary algorithm state remains inside the owning query rather than becoming public memoization substeps. There are no exempt query kinds or separately specified edge cases in this claim.

The sole implementation entry is explicitly TODO in sage_meta::todo in crates/sage-meta/tests/service_spec.rs. Its explanation says the complete public boundary inventory remains under review and per-product dependency guarantees remain incomplete. This adequately declares the entire cross-cutting guarantee deferred: it establishes none of the four obligations as implemented. The prerequisite is an audited complete public tracked-query inventory with semantic keys, independently reusable result products and dependency envelopes, including an examination of temporary state ownership. Selected well-factored queries could not establish the universal obligation, and this review does not promote such partial behavior to a whole-compiler guarantee.

The sole associated test, sage_meta::todo::crates_sage_ir_crate_semantic_query_boundaries, is an empty test with an explicit TODO. Its body calls for representative phase/subsystem key and result descriptions, permitted and forbidden dependencies, and traces excluding unrelated products and temporary public substeps. It contains no runtime assertions and supplies no behavioral verification. Its prerequisite is the audited boundary and dependency inventory declared incomplete by the implementation TODO; substantive product requests and focused traces must then assert the intended boundaries. A public query returning a broad aggregate or exposing temporary memoization state would not be detected by the current placeholder; this remains an acknowledged coverage gap, not a successful test. Both implementation and test status remain TODO. There are no ordinary or N/A entries to approve and no hidden helper calls to follow.

This assessment accepts the explicit deferral under meta.reviews.decisions, not implementation completeness. Commands executed were cargo meta review start with the saved coordinator instructions and review read for md/design/meta/reviews.md, md/design/README.md, md/design/crates/README.md and md/design/crates/sage_ir/crate.sage. No behavioral tests or build were run for this source-only review, and no production or test files were edited. All assessment source dependencies were captured. No additional edits are needed to represent the existing deferral honestly.
